newsitem.title: GERMANY: Frankfurt bourse seen catching up with IBIS gains.
newsitem.headline: Frankfurt bourse seen catching up with IBIS gains.

text.p: German shares were expected to charge ahead on Wednesday and catch up with surprise gains made in post-bourse IBIS dealings on Tuesday.

But dealers were divided on whether the 30-share DAX index would then continue to move higher or consolidate ahead of the market turbulence expected next week when shares in Deutsche Telekom are traded for the first time.

The IBIS DAX, which reflects all-day electronic dealing in the DAX, touched an all time high of 2,762.62 points, then slipped back a little to stand up 25.42 points at 2,755.86 points. The DAX had ended bourse trade at 2,734.30 points.
The IBIS DAX added over 30 points in less than an hour after Bundesbank directorate member Edgar Meister said the current dollar exchange rate of below 1.50 marks was "not appropriate".
Meister's comments boosted the dollar, which had fallen to a two month low near 1.49 marks, putting pressure on export-oriented German stocks, particularly the chemicals and auto secorts.
The December DAX future contract reached a contract high during the rally at 2,772.5, then softened slightly to stand up 25.5 points at 2,765.5 points.
Commerzbank and Deutsche Bank led the market for much of the day.
Commerzbank was heavily traded and ended up 46 pfennigs to 34.81 marks, while Deutsche Bank gained over two percent, or 1.74 marks to 70.14 marks, above the crucial 70 mark level.
Dealers said Deutsche Bank was boosted after the Oslo Stock Exchange said its investment arm Deutsche Morgan Grenfell was not obliged to bid for the Norwegian company Sysdeco Group.
The day's biggest gainer in IBIS DAX trade was Colonia Konzern, which was up 15.20 marks at 132 marks.

Colonia gained over thirteen percent after its parent company Union Assurances de Paris (UAP) said it was merging with other French insurer Axa, with analysts saying Colonia would be a key aspect in the deal.

Attention also turned to BASF AG and Veba AG, both reporting nine-month figures on Wednesday morning. BASF ended heavy IBIS trade up 1.34 points, or 2.6 percent, at 53.47 points, while Veba gained 45 pefnnigs to end IBIS dealings at 84 marks.
